name: Yed Posterior
description: A star 33 parsecs away, 10 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 79882: radius 10.019 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 54.942 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.051) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 79882: effective temperature 4968 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.044)

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 79882: distance 32.637 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.007), at which the luminosity and radius hold

limb.none: no mass is measured and no spectroscopic surface gravity is published with this radius: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770 assume the gravity of their fit (table column 15)

text.card: A star 33 parsecs away, 10 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 55 times the Sun's luminosity at 4,968 K, so 10.019 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 79882: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: Epsilon Ophiuchi
quotes.card: Epsilon Ophiuchi or ε Ophiuchi, formally named Yed Posterior, is a red giant star in the constellation of Ophiuchus.
quotes.introduction: Located less than five degrees south of the celestial equator in the eastern part of the constellation, it forms a naked eye optical double with Delta Ophiuchi.

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 4356298849169862784 (quality A), from 2018A&A...616A...7S; Gaia DR3 measures none
